name: Refugio de la Plaza Séneca, Alicante
story: Alicante, a Republican port and supply base, was bombed repeatedly by Italian aircraft from Mallorca, most deadly on 25 May 1938. The city responded with public shelters under its squares. The Plaza Séneca shelter, next to the old bus station, is one of two (with Plaza Balmis) that the city now opens as a memory site. Soundscapes recreate the experience of a raid, and a linked exhibition, 'Alicante ha caído: aquí comienza la guerra', tells the story of the city's war and its end in the port.
see: Restored underground galleries with a sound and light installation recreating an air raid.
plan: Guided visits only; book online. Tours run daily (weekday afternoons, weekend mornings) and cost €4.95. Check current times.
